commentary: Today, the DCE iron ore futures trended weaker today, with contract I2609 closing at 751.5 yuan/mt, up 0.87% from the previous trading day. Port spot prices rose 2–5 yuan/mt from the prior trading day. Trader acƟvity was moderate, and steel mills mainly purchased for essenƟal restocking. As of now, spot trading volumes were moderate. SMM's latest staƟsƟcs showed that total iron ore inventory at 35 main ports naƟonwide was 147.16 million mt, down 1.14 million mt WoW. Over the same period, the daily average port pick-up volume edged down by 23,000 mt to 3.275 million mt. This week, aﬀected by typhoons and persistent rainy weather, port operaƟons were disrupted, vessel berthing and unloading eﬃciency dropped signiﬁcantly, and port congesƟon intensiﬁed. On the demand side, as hot metal producƟon of steel mill blast furnaces conƟnued to decline, the daily average port pick-up volume pulled back slightly. With increasing blast furnace maintenance at steel mills, hot metal producƟon is sƟll expected to decline further. Therefore, from a fundamental perspec- Ɵve, short-term support for iron ore prices is expected to conƟnue weakening.
